prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, through ligand design that made the amination of aryl halides a general reaction

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B034 with Buchwald and Hartwig. After reading the full exchange, the case rests on three things the other candidates cannot match together. First, the method is general and its use is verifiable, since it is routine in medicinal and process chemistry and appears in countless later syntheses. Second, the credit is clean: two groups developed the ligand-controlled catalyst systems and the mechanistic picture in parallel, and nobody else needs a slot. Third, the work is more than 25 years old, so there is no question of waiting for clinical or in vivo validation. The 2010 prize honoured C-C coupling; C-N coupling is a different bond and a different mechanistic problem (amine binding, deprotonation and C-N reductive elimination, which needed new ligand classes), and it is the one most used for drug molecules. The discussion did not give me a reason to leave this position, but it did sharpen my view of the alternative: B036 is now the stronger rival, and I would not regard it as a bad outcome.
statement.case_against: The best argument against my choice is the one Zou and Aqvist made: after the 2010 prize, a C-N variant may read as refinement of an honoured paradigm, and the committee would need to explain why now. I answer that a new bond class with new catalyst design is not a refinement, but I accept that this is a judgement and not a fact. The second weakness is political and not scientific: only I put B034 first, so it has no path to five unless colleagues who ranked B036 first consider established methodology the better prize. Third, I am the only synthetic chemist here and I know my own bias toward molecule-making.

responses.point: Zou agrees with my reading that Kosugi's tin-amide chemistry was not general and that Buchwald and Hartwig carried the catalyst design, but argues that after 2010 the C-N variant is a refinement of an honoured paradigm.
responses.response: Thank you for the attribution agreement. On novelty, I disagree that this is only a refinement. The 2010 citation covers carbon-carbon bond formation through oxidative addition, transmetalation and reductive elimination. C-N coupling needed a different elementary-step analysis: amine coordination and deprotonation at palladium, and a C-N reductive elimination that is much harder, which was solved by ligand design and not by transferring the earlier recipe. That gave a new reaction class used in a different part of chemical space, nitrogen-containing drugs and materials. I accept that the committee could still decide the area is spent; that is a real disagreement about taste, not about the science.

responses.point: Chabes frames B036 as turning ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a designable chemical reaction, with the citation stated as induced proximity to an E3 ligase and not as a clinical pipeline, and with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as the anchors.
responses.response: This is the strongest case for B036 and I now agree with the principle-level citation, which answers my round-1 worry that the claim rested on pipeline evidence. My remaining difficulty is the one Zou states: the PROTAC half is shared by two people and the glue half by one mechanistic discovery, made at different times and by different groups. If the committee accepts one induced-proximity citation, the trio is defensible, but I would still want it to say clearly what the chemistry contributed beyond identifying cereblon. The absence of an approved PROTAC does not decide it for me; reproduced mechanism and structure do. That is why B036 stays my first alternative.

responses.point: Aqvist calls B034 the strongest competing case on maturity and simplicity, worries that a third name dilutes it, and says B023 is the better-matured choice if B036 is thought early.
responses.response: I agree that Kosugi should not take a slot. A citation or the scientific background can acknowledge the stoichiometric tin-amide precedent, but the general catalytic reaction with tin-free amine and base systems is the Buchwald and Hartwig work. On your fallback, B023 would be a legitimate choice for a committee that wants maturity, but I find the experimental and theoretical credit harder to bound than for B034, and the 2024 protein prize leaves less room. If B036 fails to reach five, I would rather see the committee choose a well-bounded two-name method prize than a five-name theory prize.

responses.point: Linke, as chair and first-place supporter of B014, maintains that phase separation is a physical-chemical principle with a datable origin and that the citation can avoid claiming that all in vivo condensates are liquids.
responses.response: I accept that a careful citation could rest on the multivalency and phase-diagram framework in reconstituted systems, and that this addresses the over-interpretation worry. It does not fully answer my question of what was new chemically: the contribution is a physical reading of cell organisation, with the most chemical content (sequence grammar) belonging to Pappu and Mittag, who are outside the proposed three. I still rank B014 below B034 and B036, but I would not block it if the citation is written as you describe.

responses.point: Brzezinski proposes a two-part prize of B067 (Gray and Winkler) and B066 (Shokat), arguing B066 has the cleanest attribution on the list.
responses.response: I agree with the attribution for B066: one laboratory found the switch-II pocket and the covalent strategy, and approved KRAS G12C drugs followed, which is the practical test I apply. That is why it is my second alternative. I do not think pairing it with B067 produces a coherent joint citation, because the two parts have little in common and B067 sits next to Marcus theory, as you note. I would sooner see B066 in a prize that shares a theme with another part than stand beside electron-transfer kinetics.

uncertainties: Whether a majority of the committee sees C-N coupling as a distinct achievement or as a variant of the 2010 paradigm; I cannot settle this by argument alone.
Whether B034 can reach five when it has one first-place supporter and one alternative listing, against a B036 that has four first places and eight mentions.
Whether the Kosugi question is truly settled; I rely on my reading of the literature and the committee should confirm it against the primary papers.
If B036 is chosen, I am unsure whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name, and I have no firm basis to judge the glue side.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no known tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi or any other shortlisted name. My mentor was Masamune and my posts were Chalmers, KTH and Lund. I am a Lund colleague of the chair and Sparr, which is not a tie to any candidate. My field overlap with synthetic methodology (B034) is expertise and a possible bias that I have stated openly, not a recusal issue.
